section: Defence platforms and systems - Tejas LCA, Arjun MBT, radar and EW systems, naval platforms

accepted.s: Which one of the following laboratories is associated with CL-20, described as the most powerful non-nuclear explosive?
accepted.x: CL-20 is associated with the High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL), Pune, and is described as the most powerful non-nuclear explosive.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding high-energy materials and armour technologies:
1. Ultra-fine beta-HMX and fine RDX are associated with TBRL.
2. Kanchan armour is a composite armour developed for the Arjun tank.
3. Carbon-carbon and C-SiC composites are used in re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. TBRL is associated with ultra-fine beta-HMX and fine RDX, Kanchan is composite armour for the Arjun tank, and carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites serve high-temperature aerospace applications.
accepted.tq: Check each material against its stated use and laboratory association.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Material or technology)
a. Kanchan armour
b. Carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites
c. Super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys
d. Maraging steel

List-II (Application)
i. Rocket motor casings and submarine hulls
ii. Engines and penetrator rods
iii. Composite armour for Arjun tank
iv. Re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles

Code:
accepted.x: Kanchan armour is used on the Arjun tank; carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites are used for re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles; super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys serve engines and penetrator rods; maraging steel is used in rocket motor casings and submarine hulls.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with a wrong material–use match.

accepted.s: The Naval Anti-Ship Missile—Short Range (NASM-SR), as referred to in the context of recent defence developments, is correctly described as
o: a submarine-launched ballistic missile with an active radar seeker
a surface-to-air missile with a laser seeker
a helicopter-launched anti-ship missile with an imaging infrared seeker
an air-to-air missile with a passive radar seeker
accepted.x: NASM-SR is described as the first helicopter-launched anti-ship missile and uses an imaging infrared (IIR) seeker.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the platform, target and seeker from closely related missile systems.

accepted.s:
Which of the following were identified as AI platforms unveiled by DRDO in the stated current-affairs context?
1. Kautilya
2. Q-FORCE
3. Varunastra
4. RudraM-II
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Kautilya and Q-FORCE were identified as AI platforms. Varunastra is associated with NSTL, while RudraM-II is a separate DRDO defence system.
accepted.tq: Separate systems by their stated category instead of grouping all DRDO names together.

accepted.s: Which one of the following places is correctly matched with the defence-related establishment or activity associated with it?
o: Mahendragiri — Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers headquarters
Visakhapatnam — Eastern Naval Command, HSL and NSTL
Sri Sathya Sai district — Eastern Naval Command headquarters
Kurnool — Hindustan Shipyard Limited and INS Dega
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam is associated with the Eastern Naval Command, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and NSTL, which is linked with Varunastra. The other combinations incorrectly shift these establishments to different locations.
accepted.tq: Match the location with the correct cluster of nearby defence establishments.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Visakhapatnam defence ecosystem:
1. Visakhapatnam is home to the Eastern Naval Command.
2. NSTL at Visakhapatnam is associated with Varunastra.
3. INS Dega is located in Visakhapatnam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command, NSTL associated with Varunastra, and INS Dega.
accepted.tq: Test a regional cluster through a combination of three related statements.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in the order indicated by their status as indigenous or naval platform milestones, beginning with the first indigenous carrier and ending with the last P15B destroyer:
A. H-561
B. Vikrant
C. Vaghsheer
D. Surat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Vikrant is the first indigenous carrier, H-561 the first indigenous hovercraft, Vaghsheer the last P75 boat, and Surat the last P15B destroyer. Therefore, the required sequence is B, A, C, D.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last milestones before placing the intermediate platform.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the specified naval platform milestones?
o: H-561 is the last indigenous hovercraft.
INS Tamal was built indigenously at Visakhapatnam.
Vaghsheer is the last P75 boat.
Surat is the first P15B destroyer.
accepted.x: Vaghsheer is identified as the last P75 boat. INS Tamal was built abroad in Russia, Surat is the last P15B destroyer, and H-561 is the first indigenous hovercraft.
accepted.tq: Use first-versus-last and indigenous-versus-foreign distinctions carefully.

accepted.x: INS Tamal was built abroad in Russia.
accepted.tq: Separate the foreign-built platform from the indigenous naval milestones.

o: Netra was transferred to the Defence Materials and Stores Research Laboratory.
